title: BER Flight Delay Compensation - Quick Summary
items: **Three hours late at the far end, not at the gate.** Compensation starts when your arrival at the final destination is three hours or more behind schedule. A four hour wait in Berlin that still lands on time pays nothing.

**250, 400 or 600 euro, decided by distance.** Up to 1,500 kilometres is 250 euro. Above that it is 400 euro, and 600 euro is reserved for long flights that leave the EU. Of the 157 destinations BER serves, 79 pay 250, 69 pay 400 and only 9 reach 600.
**The Canaries are the classic trap.** Tenerife South is 3,669 kilometres from Berlin, but it is an intra-EU flight, so it is worth 400 euro and never 600. Dubai at 4,613 kilometres is worth 600.

**Food, drinks and a hotel are owed even when money is not.** The right to care starts at two, three or four hours depending on distance, and it survives fog, strikes and air traffic control failures. Past five hours you can walk away and demand a refund.
**Never take a voucher instead of cash.** You are entitled to a bank transfer. Giving up a seat voluntarily on an overbooked flight also cancels your rights.

**The July 2026 EU reform does not apply yet.** Parliament approved it on 7 July 2026 and the Council on 13 July, but it starts in 2027. The three hour rule and the 250, 400 and 600 euro amounts survived unchanged anyway.

**Going into the city is easy.** The station is directly under Terminal 1, the Airport Express reaches Hauptbahnhof in 22 minutes and Alexanderplatz in about 32, and an ABC ticket is 5.00 euro single or 12.90 euro for 24 hours.
